messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency > SLO (prod-cluster-3). Metric: request_latency_p99=820ms (SLO=500ms). Spike correlated with kv_cache_evictions and slab_fragmentation. Auto-runbooks triggered: paging to eng-sre.

sam (eng-oncall): saw this, joining. I can repro tail spikes on streaming endpoints (chat/stream). p95 also creeping up ~320ms.

maria (sre): any customer-facing errors? Nate?

nate (customer-ops): a handful of live sessions reported stalls and missing stream chunks, intermittent. Not widespread but customer SLA-relevant. Escalating to support.

sam (eng-oncall): attaching quick top output from cluster master:
```
# node stats summary (prod-cluster-3)
kv_cache_evictions_total: 124k
kv_cache_frag_ratio: 0.67
streaming_stalls/sec: 4.2
prefill_requests/sec: 540
decode_requests/sec: 180
```

sam (eng-oncall): note prefill vs decode imbalance ~3:1. That matches previous tail stalls when prefill floods KV and decode can't keep up, causing slab thrash.

henry (runtime): yep, we've seen fragmentation when prefill writes many small entries. Slab allocs get fragmented -> lookup/decode slows -> tail latency.

maria (sre): immediate mitigation suggestions?

henry (runtime): short-term: reduce prefill rate, increase slab reclaim threshold, and enable targeted eviction for high-frag slabs. I can push a runtime flag. Longer term: dynamic slab compaction.

jenna (platform): is it safe to route some traffic to fallback VM group with larger shard size? We can flip routing per policy. That will increase cost but reduce customer impact.

sam (eng-oncall): propose plan: 1) apply runtime flag to lower prefill throttle to 60% of normal. 2) enable targeted eviction on top 10% fragmented slabs. 3) open a routing rule to send 20% of streaming traffic to fallback group. 4) monitor p95/p99 and streaming_stalls.

maria (sre): +1. Assigning tasks: henry takes runtime flag + eviction, jenna takes routing, sam will monitor and coordinate. Nate to brief customers.

henry (runtime): applying runtime change now: `rbctl set runtime.kv.prefill_rate_limit 0.6 --cluster prod-cluster-3`
henry (runtime): enabling targeted eviction for slabs with frag_ratio > 0.6: `rbctl kv eviction set-target --cluster prod-cluster-3 --threshold 0.6 --top 10%`

henry (runtime): done. Patch rollout on 3/3 serving nodes first. Watching.

jenna (platform): creating routing override: `routectl set policy streaming --cluster prod-cluster-3 --fallback-group pg-fallback-2 --percent 20`
jenna (platform): applied.

sam (eng-oncall): metrics 2m after changes:
```
request_latency_p99: 610ms -> 430ms (post changes)
request_latency_p95: 320ms -> 210ms
streaming_stalls/sec: 4.2 -> 0.9
kv_cache_evictions_total delta: dropping rate by ~70%
kv_cache_frag_ratio: 0.67 -> 0.58 (start of compaction)
```

sam (eng-oncall): looks promising. Continuing to monitor. Leaving oncall but handing to maria for next shift.

maria (sre): taking handoff. Sam, please add runbook steps to the thread (short) and link jump box logs.

sam (eng-oncall): runbook snippet: 
- If p99 > SLO: reduce prefill rate to 50% and route 30% to fallback.
- Run `rbctl kv eviction status --cluster <cluster>` and target slabs with frag_ratio > 0.6.
- If streaming_stalls persist: temporarily scale dedicated pool by +1 node.
- Notify customers via support if >5% sessions affected for >10m.

nate (customer-ops): communicating to impacted customers now. Template: "We're mitigating a service degradation causing intermittent streaming stalls; we've applied mitigations and expect improvement; we'll follow up with a postmortem."

maria (sre): a few follow-ups: 1) trigger runbook job to compact slabs overnight; 2) schedule postmortem with runtime and platform. Henry, please capture exact flags changed and config diffs. Jenna, capture routing change id. Sam, add the monitoring dashboards + alert thresholds updated.

henry (runtime): capturing: changed `runtime.kv.prefill_rate_limit` 0.6 -> was 1.0, enabled `kv.eviction.target_threshold=0.6`, eviction policy set to "frag-first" for targeted slabs. Patch PR created: #4893.

jenna (platform): routing change id: route-policy-20260312-17. I also left rollback command: `routectl rollback route-policy-20260312-17`

sam (eng-oncall): quick note: we saw one hotspot on shard-18 where decode threads saturated leading to per-request blocking. Increased decode worker pool by 2 on that host as a temporary fix. Command: `sysctl set decode.workers=10` (applied).

maria (sre): thanks. Initial incident classification: Sev 2 (customer-impacting latency, partial). Postmortem owners: maria (lead), henry (runtime), jenna (platform).

nate (customer-ops): customers notified. Will collect any additional impact reports and feed into postmortem.

sam (eng-oncall): leaving note: keep an eye on `kv_cache_frag_ratio` and `prefill:decode` ratio. If frag_ratio stops decreasing after 30m, escalate to emergency scale and full fallback.

maria (sre): acknowledged. Monitoring will stay on for next 2 hours and then hand to routine ops. I'll open a postmortem doc and link here when ready.

incident-bot: AUTOMATED NOTE: runbook step executed by henry (runtime) at 8176543312; jenna applied routing change at 8176543350.

maria (sre): final note for thread: mitigations restored p99 under SLO for now, keeping this open until frag ratio stable <0.55 and streaming_stalls <1/min for 1h.

nate (customer-ops): will send a follow-up to customers once we have stable metrics for 1h.

sam (eng-oncall): thanks team, good quick triage.

henry (runtime): adding logs and minor perf traces to PR for deeper root cause analysis (prefill burst patterns + allocator behavior).

maria (sre): closing handoff. Postmortem owners please post link and timeline here when ready.

jenna (platform): noted. I'll add the routing playbook to for future automated failovers.

incident-bot: THREAD STATUS: open -> monitoring (assigned: maria (sre)).
